themes_detail.label: Street Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints spiked to 4 this week, a 700% increase from the 0.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting either a sudden enforcement crackdown, new vendor activity, or community frustration over street commerce in Sheepshead Bay/Gravesend.
evidence: 4 vendor enforcement complaints filed this week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 4.95)
Statistically significant anomaly appearing at the very edge of the monitoring window
No prior Reddit or local news mentions suggest this is an emerging, under-reported issue
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD or Parks enforcement to understand what triggered the sudden spike in complaints
Speak with street vendors and business owners in Sheepshead Bay about enforcement pressure or new vendor arrivals

themes_detail.label: Tree Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 2 weeks, complaints about dead/dying trees and overgrown branches have accelerated dramatically—10 dead/dying tree complaints last week (371% above baseline) and 16 overgrown branch complaints 2 weeks ago (327% above baseline)—pointing to a deteriorating street tree canopy ahead of the growing season.
evidence: 10 dead/dying tree complaints last week vs. 2.1 weekly average (371% spike, z-score: 5.13)
16 overgrown tree/branch complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.8 weekly average (327% spike, z-score: 5.99)
Both spikes converge on the same underlying issue: tree maintenance backlog or disease outbreak
reporting_angles: Request data from Parks Department on tree maintenance schedules and disease monitoring in CD 315
Walk affected blocks to document visual evidence; interview residents about safety concerns from overhanging branches

themes_detail.label: Building Maintenance Backlog
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints jumped 300% last week (11 complaints vs. 2.8 weekly average), suggesting a surge in building system failures, deferred maintenance, or code compliance issues affecting residential or commercial properties in the district.
evidence: 11 maintenance/facility complaints last week vs. 2.8 weekly average (300% spike, z-score: 5.58)
Complements the persistent heat/hot water issue (1,045 complaints over 90 days, 4th highest category)
585 DOB alteration permits filed in 90 days may indicate older building stock undergoing reactive repairs rather than proactive upgrades
reporting_angles: Cross-reference maintenance spikes with DOB permit data to identify properties with recurring violations
Interview residents in older buildings to understand what systems are failing (heat, plumbing, electrical)

themes_detail.label: Elevator System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints peaked 3 weeks ago with a 1500% spike (4 complaints vs. 0.2 weekly average, z-score: 8.66), the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset, indicating either a temporary surge in building elevator outages or a single widespread failure affecting multiple units.
evidence: 4 elevator complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score: 8.66, highest severity in dataset)
Spike has already cooled, suggesting either a resolved incident or cyclical maintenance pattern
No follow-up complaints in most recent week indicates problem may have been addressed or was isolated
reporting_angles: Determine if spike was from a single building or district-wide elevator maintenance/safety issue
Contact DOB to check inspection records and violations for multi-unit residential buildings around the spike date

themes_detail.label: Homelessness & Encampment Growth
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints spiked 367% two weeks ago (7 complaints vs. 1.5 weekly average), reflecting a concentrated homeless encampment issue in public spaces, parks, or vacant lots in Sheepshead Bay/Gravesend.
evidence: 7 encampment complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.5 weekly average (367% spike, z-score: 4.92)
Converges with spike in park noise complaints 3 weeks ago (3 vs. 0.9 baseline, 243% increase)
Suggests encampment activity concentrated in public spaces; may reflect seasonal migration or service gap
reporting_angles: Locate and document encampments; interview residents and business owners about safety and sanitation concerns
Contact NYC DHS and NYPD Homeless Outreach Unit to learn about services, outreach efforts, and why numbers spiked
